summary: The observed do/don’t crossover is real in its measured conditions, but neither parameter count nor the labels compact, strong and frontier supply universal thresholds.

points.text: Fan et al. is a September 2026 preprint. Its tool intervention changes the tool registry, interface prompt, file-state tracking and post-edit diagnostics together; it does not isolate tool count or prove a generally optimal Bash interface.

The crossover was measured for three Nemotron-3 sizes and one Mistral model. The authors warn that model size is an imperfect capability proxy; Terminal-Bench has 89 tasks and many individual contrasts lack significance.

A recommendation can flip by task even for the same model: in LongCodeBench, retrieval hurt Claude 3.5 Sonnet’s repository QA but improved its long-context patching at 256k. This single-shot benchmark should not be transferred untested to interactive agents.

A small scaffold study found up to 40-fold variation in tokens per solved task across harnesses but mostly statistically inconclusive accuracy differences. Cost, latency and reliability need separate reporting.
